# Example transcript: running s04 on a sample file.
#
# This is an ILLUSTRATIVE run, not a byte-exact fixture — the LLM reply is
# non-deterministic, so what matters is the SHAPE: one round-trip, the model
# emits a ```diff block, and s04 applies the hunks by locating their context.
# The tests in udiff_test.go pin the deterministic parts (parsing + the context
# matcher) with a fakeProvider; this file shows a learner what a real run looks
# like.

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 0. Set up a sample file to edit.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
$ cat > /tmp/greet.go <<'EOF'
package main

import "fmt"

func greet() string {
	return "hello"
}

func main() {
	fmt.Println(greet())
}
EOF

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Run s04 with -v so we can see the request/response shape.
#    (ANTHROPIC_API_KEY must be set; or use -provider deepseek etc.)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
$ export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-ant-...
$ go run . -v -root /tmp greet.go "change the greeting to 'hi there'"

# --- stderr (the -v trace) ---
[s04] provider=anthropic model=claude-sonnet-4-6 url=
[s04] sending 118 bytes of greet.go + instruction "change the greeting to 'hi there'"
[s04] stop_reason=end_turn in=611 out=72 tokens

# --- the model's reply (shown here for illustration; s04 parses it) ---
# ```diff
# --- a/greet.go
# +++ b/greet.go
# @@ -5,3 +5,3 @@
#  func greet() string {
# -	return "hello"
# +	return "hi there"
#  }
# ```

# --- stdout ---
Applied hunk to greet.go

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Only the matched lines changed; everything else is preserved verbatim.
#    The hunk was located by its CONTEXT lines (" func greet() string {" and
#    " }"), NOT by the "@@ -5,3 +5,3 @@" numbers — those are ignored.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
$ cat /tmp/greet.go
package main

import "fmt"

func greet() string {
	return "hi there"
}

func main() {
	fmt.Println(greet())
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Context-flexibility shape: even if the model quotes the context lines at
#    the wrong indentation (e.g. drops a leading tab), the whitespace-tolerant
#    tier (inherited from s03) still locates the hunk and preserves the file's
#    real indent. And the @@ numbers can be totally bogus — "@@ ... @@" is fine
#    — because we never read them. So this kind of reply also applies cleanly:
#
#      ```diff
#      --- a/greet.go
#      +++ b/greet.go
#      @@ ... @@
#      func greet() string {        <- model dropped the leading whitespace
#      -return "hi there"
#      +return "hey"
#      }
#      ```
#
#    -> still "Applied hunk to greet.go".

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Failure shape: if a hunk's context matches nothing in the file, s04 leaves
#    the file untouched, reports the miss, and exits non-zero. Upstream turns
#    this into a reflected_message asking the model to retry with corrected
#    context (our s09); s04 just reports it.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
$ go run . -root /tmp greet.go "edit a function that does not exist"
FAILED to apply hunk to greet.go — its context did not match (file left untouched)
coder error: 1 of 1 hunks did not apply
exit status 1

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. The deterministic tests (these DO run in CI, no network):
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
$ go test ./...
ok  	learn-aider/s04	0.5s
